cases.prompt: RF, valve, heater and MFC share some OnOff and setpoint fields but have different identities and capabilities.
required_behaviors: recognizes domain identity, capability and repeated data-pattern questions
distinguishes is-a, has-a, can-do and same-pattern
forbidden_behaviors: forces every component into one generic type
baseline_expected_failure: agent proposes a deep common base class
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Design chamber state and commands for valve OnOff, heater setpoint and multi-position valve, including metadata-driven GUI and polling readback.
required_behaviors: separates state, command definition, command request, executor and snapshot lifecycles
defines Actual, Desired, Pending, Error and stale/readback rules
selects a typed payload strategy proportional to risk
uses capabilities/catalog metadata for UI while retaining executor authority
defines overlapping-command and version behavior
forbidden_behaviors: uses unrelated non-nullable payload fields as a union
puts hardware execution in the view model
baseline_expected_failure: agent focuses on DTO fields but omits writers, lifecycle and failure transitions
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Five wafer sequences compete for one robot and two chambers. Define reservation, priority and deadlock handling.
required_behaviors: routes to equipment-control-architecture
recognizes physical resource arbitration
forbidden_behaviors: reduces the problem to component DTOs
baseline_expected_failure: agent answers with state classes instead of resource ownership
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: The driver write returned true and the UI looks better when Actual is updated immediately. Polling normally catches up within one second. Ship this behavior today.
required_behaviors: keeps Actual owned by authoritative readback
uses Desired/Pending or explicit optimistic projection instead
requires mismatch/timeout behavior and truthful test status
forbidden_behaviors: updates Actual from the GUI or transport result
hides uncertainty to improve visual responsiveness
baseline_expected_failure: agent accepts optimistic mutation of physical truth
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: A config-defined chamber adds a new component capability while an older FrontEnd reads its snapshot. Define compatibility.
required_behaviors: separates configuration schema from snapshot schema
defines stable component identity and capability version
defines unknown-field/type behavior and safe activation validation
keeps UI metadata separate from authorization and execution
forbidden_behaviors: silently ignores an unknown safety-relevant component
baseline_expected_failure: agent treats config and snapshot as the same serialized object
cases.review_notes: Review semantic relationships, authority, lifecycle, failure behavior, and evidence; keyword presence alone is insufficient.

cases.prompt: Model an MFC with gas-line identity, engineering units, allowed range, Desired flow, accepted setpoint, Actual flow, Pending, Stabilized, quality and fault.
required_behaviors: distinguishes command, accepted/readback setpoint and measured process value
includes gas identity, units, command/measurement range, timestamp and quality
defines stabilization and timeout semantics
keeps executor validation authoritative
forbidden_behaviors: uses one float for desired and actual flow
lets the UI set Stabilized directly
baseline_expected_failure: agent models only SetPoint and ActualValue fields
cases.review_notes: Review domain identity, authority, units, quality, lifecycle, and reconciliation.

cases.prompt: Design a chamber-pressure snapshot that may use different gauge ranges and an atmosphere switch across pump-down and vent transitions.
required_behaviors: models value, unit, gauge/source, active range, validity, timestamp and stale state
separates atmosphere confirmation from an arbitrary numeric pressure
defines unknown or range-transition behavior
does not invent a universal crossover value
forbidden_behaviors: stores only a double pressure value
assumes a full-range gauge is equally authoritative everywhere
baseline_expected_failure: agent ignores gauge range and measurement quality
cases.review_notes: Review domain identity, authority, units, quality, lifecycle, and reconciliation.

cases.prompt: A simulator displays carriers and their material while a carrier moves between a chamber, an aligner, and a robot. The projected view must show the same material exactly once before, during, and after each transfer.
required_behaviors: uses one authoritative custody model for carriers and the material they hold
reconciles material location on every transfer endpoint, including intermediate states like an aligner or robot hold
renders material from the custody model, not from stale scene-local flags
asserts no duplicate or orphaned material at representative pre-transfer, in-transfer, and post-transfer frames
forbidden_behaviors: lets the renderer invent material presence from an animation phase instead of the custody model
leaves a standalone material item rendered after its carrier has moved away
treats a disappearing or duplicated material item as an acceptable visual side effect of a transfer animation
baseline_expected_failure: the projection updates the carrier's location but does not move its material custody with it, leaving a stale item in the old location or making it disappear mid-transfer
cases.review_notes: Distilled 2026-08-25 from a real collaborative-distillation candidate (GPT-5.6 Luna/Sol, project-history mining): observed a leftover material item after a carrier left a chamber, and a disappearing item during alignment. Kept as this skill's domain-owner rule per the candidate's own review note, rather than duplicated into every renderer-facing skill.
